title: Grandpa Eliezer and the Stubborn Carrot
summary: In Grandpa Eliezer's garden grows a carrot as big as an elephant, and it will not come out of the ground. Grandma, the granddaughter, a goat in boots, a bear with an umbrella and seven frogs all come to pull. A rhyming story with a repeating line that is fun to join in.
pages:
In Grandpa Eliezer's garden
a carrot grew and grew.
Not a little one, not an ordinary one,
an ENORMOUS one, as big as an elephant, too!

"What a carrot!" Grandpa said,
"I'll cook a feast before bed!"
He grabbed the leaves and pulled with both hands.
He pulled and he pulled, with all of his might!
And the carrot? Still stuck in the ground, holding tight.

Grandpa called: "Grandma, come help me, please!
I can't move this carrot all by myself with ease!"
Grandma held Grandpa, Grandpa held the carrot.
They pulled and they pulled, with all of their might!
And the carrot? Still stuck in the ground, holding tight.

Grandma called her granddaughter: "Put down your doll!
Come help us pull, it's the most important job of all!"
Granddaughter held Grandma, Grandma held Grandpa, Grandpa held the carrot.
They pulled and they pulled, with all of their might!
And the carrot? Still stuck in the ground, holding tight.

The granddaughter called the goat in boots,
who came hopping on two legs, skipping over the roots.
Goat held Granddaughter, Granddaughter held Grandma,
Grandma held Grandpa, Grandpa held the carrot.
They pulled and they pulled, with all of their might!
And the carrot? Still stuck in the ground, holding tight.

The goat called the bear with the umbrella,
who was eating cake in the library, what a fella!
Bear held Goat, Goat held Granddaughter, Granddaughter held Grandma,
Grandma held Grandpa, Grandpa held the carrot.
They pulled and they pulled, with all of their might!
And the carrot? Still stuck in the ground, holding tight.

The bear called seven frogs
who sat on a fence, singing songs by the logs.
Frogs held Bear, Bear held Goat, Goat held Granddaughter,
Granddaughter held Grandma, Grandma held Grandpa, Grandpa held the carrot.
They pulled and they pulled, with all of their might!
And the carrot? It wiggled a little... no.
Still stuck in the ground, holding tight.

Everyone sat down. Everyone huffed and puffed.
"This carrot is strange!" said Eliezer. "It's tough!
Is it glued? Is it locked?
Is someone down there, holding on under the rocks?"

Then, from under a leaf, came a tiny voice:
"Maybe I can help? I'm here, I'm your choice!"
Who is it? An ant! As small as a crumb.
Everyone laughed: "You? You can't help, little one!"

But the ant grabbed hold of the very last frog.
Ant held Frogs, Frogs held Bear,
Bear held Goat, Goat held Granddaughter, Granddaughter held Grandma,
Grandma held Grandpa, Grandpa held the carrot.
They pulled and they pulled, with all of their might...

POP!
Out came the carrot, it flew through the air!
And everyone fell backwards: BOOM, CRASH, SPLAT, everywhere!

What do you do with a carrot this tall?
You invite everyone, there's enough for all!
Carrot soup for Grandpa, carrot cake for Bear.
And the ant? She got a crumb. And she was the happiest one there.
